title: Choose the visual world for AiFoundIt search (re-roll 1)
question: Fresh set. The roll assigned Pocket Field Notebook. Each preview is a hand-built HTML mock of the chat screen, not a generated image.

options.label: Pocket Field Notebook
options.lineage: Rhodia and Field Notes pocket memo books: orange cover, violet dot grid
options.thesis: A private notebook only you carry. Your questions are entries; found files are taped onto the page.
options.viewport: Orange cover band as the top app bar. Below it, a pencil-filled index bar, your question as a large entry with its time in the margin, the reply with two taped-in screenshots, and a checklist-style move proposal.
options.risk: The tape can tip into scrapbook kitsch. It has to stay limited to found files.

raised.raise: Fixed fields: every taped-in file shows the same caption fields in the same order (type · date, then folder).
Tapping a file brings it forward and dims the rest of the page, revealing the 'why it matched' note. That is how reasons appear on demand.
Ink is never pure black and the paper never pure white, so the page reads as printed.
Nothing is labeled twice: no 'AI' badges and no repeated status chips. The margin timestamp is the only metadata a chat entry gets.

options.label: Lost Property Counter
options.lineage: Lost-and-found claim stubs and manila luggage tags
options.thesis: You describe what you lost; the counter hands back a numbered claim ticket with your items tagged.
options.viewport: Each reply is a red claim stub with a number. The files hang below it as manila tags, and a dashed slip proposes shelving them.
options.risk: It's the literal reading of the name 'AiFoundIt', and the joke could wear thin.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.lineage: Airport signage: yellow bands, black humanist type
options.thesis: Every answer is a sign: where your files are, how many, and which way to go.
options.viewport: A yellow band names the folder and shows the match count at large size. The files sit beneath it, and a move proposal is a second sign.
options.case: Wins on clarity (location and count read instantly), but it's colder for a personal, privacy-focused app.
options.risk: Can feel like a transit app, not a personal one.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Files are coupons with ruled fields; organizing actions get stamped PENDING, VALIDATED, or VOID, and nothing silently disappears.
options.viewport: The files are perforated coupons with date, type, and folder fields. The move proposal is stamped PENDING until you validate it.
options.case: Its stamp system matches 'never auto-delete or move' exactly, but it's a rarer reference for everyday users.
options.risk: The form-heavy layout is dense in long chats.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Results as board rows that flip into place.
options.viewport: A board of file rows above the composer.
options.case: Loses on both: rows of text hide the thumbnails people use to recognize their files.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.lineage: Printed design annuals with registration marks
options.thesis: Files presented as plates with registration crosshairs.
options.viewport: Plate grid with a credits row.
options.case: Loses on both: gallery-like, with nothing everyday about it.
options.kept: Never pure black, never pure white.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Results in horizontal rows; the focused file expands.
options.case: Loses on both: built for browsing, not for finding one file.
options.kept: Focus brings the file forward and dims the rest.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.viewport: A catalog number instead of a reply line.
options.case: Loses on both: labels encoded as color blocks work against calm clarity.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard AI chat app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The chat layout people already expect, with files as attachment rows.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Gemini or ChatGPT by design.
